headline: NORDIQUE KWYJIBO PEA ADVANCED: NQC Submits REE Assessment to TSX-V — 8.48Mt @ 2.45% TREO Eyes SEDAR Filing Late August
source_name: GlobeNewswire / Nordique Critical Metals Inc. (TSX-V: NQC)
snippet: Nordique Critical Metals Inc. (TSX-V: NQC) announced August 12 that it has submitted its preliminary economic assessment technical report to the TSX Venture Exchange, completing a required condition for closing its option to earn up to an 80% interest in the Kwyjibo Rare Earth Project in Quebec — with a SEDAR+ filing of the PEA expected in late August 2026. The project's mineral resource stands at 8.48 million tonnes grading 2.45% total rare earth oxides (Measured and Indicated) plus 1.825 million tonnes at 3.27% TREO (Inferred), with a notably uncommon distribution in which 45.5% of the TREO falls into the 'critical REO' classification that carries the highest strategic premium in the Western supply chain. For rare earth investors, Kwyjibo's high critical-REO fraction — heavily weighted toward neodymium, praseodymium, and terbium rather than the cerium and lanthanum that dominate most deposits — combined with its Quebec jurisdiction and the PEA's imminent public availability, makes this the catalytic document that transforms Kwyjibo from a resource estimate into a project with disclosed project economics.

headline: TIER ONE SILVER RAISES C$12-17M: 70% CONTROL STAKE IN ECUADOR'S GIANT RUTA DE COBRE COPPER-MOLY PROJECT
source_name: Newsfile Corp / Tier One Silver Inc. (TSX-V: TSLV)
snippet: Tier One Silver Inc. (TSX-V: TSLV) announced August 13 it has engaged 3L Capital Inc. as lead agent for a best-efforts private placement targeting C$12–17 million at C$0.07 per unit (each unit comprising one share and one three-year warrant at C$0.15), with the minimum net proceeds of US$1.8 million allocated to the initial purchase payment for a 70% control option over Compañía Minera Ruta de Cobre S.A. — described as one of South America's largest greenfield copper-molybdenum mineral projects, located in Azuay Province, Ecuador, with the offering targeted to close in early September 2026. For junior investors tracking explorers pivoting to copper in the current cycle: Tier One Silver is effectively repositioning its treasury capital toward one of the continent's most prospective copper-moly footprints at a moment when copper sustained above $6.50/lb is making Ecuador's Andean copper belt one of the most watched jurisdictions for undeveloped porphyry copper systems — the 70% control stake structure preserves upside while limiting initial capital at risk.

headline: CONQUEST CQR: 15.31 g/t Au AT SMITH LAKE ONTARIO — Campbell Vein Adjacent to Barrick's Historic 1M-oz Renabie Mine
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Conquest Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: CQR)
snippet: Conquest Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: CQR) reported August 12 the first surface channel sampling results from its Smith Lake Gold Project in Ontario — 15 channel samples from the Campbell Vein collected during a June 2026 field visit returned grades ranging from 0.03 to 29.10 g/t gold, with 6 of 15 samples above 1 g/t and a highlighted result of 15.31 g/t gold over 3.00 metres; the company is now planning an approximate 500-sample B-horizon geochemical survey this fall to systematically trace the gold-bearing stratigraphy north-northeast of the known Smith Lake Gold Zone. Smith Lake's strategic context is significant: the project sits adjacent to Barrick Mining Corp.'s former Renabie Gold Mine, which produced more than 1,000,000 ounces of gold at 6.6 g/t over 50 years — and channel sampling that confirms comparable grades in the Campbell Vein at Smith Lake is the first step toward understanding whether Conquest holds additional analogous mineralization in the same geological environment at a gold price of $4,350/oz.

headline: PROSPECTIVA RESOURCES LISTS TSX-V TODAY: Fully Funded Brazil Copper-Gold Drill Begins at São Francisco
snippet: Prospectiva Resources Ltd. (TSX-V: PSVA) began trading on the TSX Venture Exchange on August 14, 2026, bringing public market liquidity to a Brazil-focused copper and gold exploration company whose fully funded drill program commenced in early August at the São Francisco Copper-Gold Project, designed to expand high-grade, near-surface copper-gold mineralization beyond the historical resource boundary. São Francisco is located in Brazil's prolific copper-gold corridor in Pará State, a jurisdiction that has hosted several multi-million-ounce gold discoveries and significant copper-gold porphyry systems in the past decade. For retail investors following new TSX-V listings: Prospectiva's distinction is the simultaneous exchange debut and active drill program — providing public market access to a copper-gold system at the exact moment first-hole results are being generated, eliminating the typical lag between listing and drilling that characterizes most newly public explorers.

headline: KALKINE: BUYING MID-TIER GOLD IN AUGUST — Pan American's $1.7B Cash, IAMGOLD +28% on Buybacks, Alamos's Grade Recovery Path
snippet: Kalkine Canada's August 2026 analysis of mid-tier precious metals companies examines four stocks through the lens of Q2 2026 results and current commodity prices: Pan American Silver (TSX: PAAS) leads on balance-sheet strength with US$1.6–1.8 billion in cash and a record C$300 million in total shareholder returns last quarter, establishing it as the sector's clearest fortress play; IAMGOLD (TSX: IMG) surged 28.8% post-Q2 on the combination of $507.3M adjusted EBITDA, an aggressive C$510M buyback program since December 2025, and the Côté Gold mine returning to near-full throughput after conveyor replacement — the kind of operational-plus-financial-improvement combination that historically drives sustained re-rating; Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI) carries a production wobble from Young-Davidson's June seismic event but remains the sector's cleanest Canadian-jurisdictional franchise with record Island Gold output; Endeavour Mining (TSX: EDV) posted $392M Q2 adjusted net earnings but sits furthest out on the risk curve, with 100% West Africa exposure where resource nationalism is described as 'a present-tense policy reality.' For retail investors choosing entry points in gold mining in August 2026, Kalkine's framework separates capital-return capacity (Pan American, IAMGOLD) from operational-recovery narratives (Alamos) and geopolitical discount stories (Endeavour).

headline: KALKINE ON SILVER STOCKS AUGUST: Endeavour Silver +148% Revenue, Silvercorp Steady, Allied Gold M&A Premium at $64/oz
snippet: Kalkine Canada's August 2026 silver mining stock analysis focuses on four companies offering distinct ways to hold silver exposure at $64/oz: Endeavour Silver Corp. (TSX: EDR) delivered Q2 2026 revenue of $212.1 million versus $85.3 million in Q2 2025 — a 148% surge powered by the addition of Terronera and a full quarter of Kolpa operations, with mine operating earnings of $74.0 million versus $7.7 million — making it the clearest single-quarter demonstration of what new-mine additions do to a silver miner's cash flow at elevated silver prices; Silvercorp Metals (TSX: SVM) offers a consistently profitable, low-cost Chinese silver-lead-zinc operation for investors seeking stable, dividend-paying silver exposure without construction or development risk; Predictive Discovery provides leveraged exploration upside in West African gold-silver; Allied Gold (TSX: AAUC) carries an M&A premium following strategic interest that was publicly disclosed. For silver-focused retail investors: the Kalkine screening of these four companies illustrates how the silver mining universe stratifies at $64/oz — between operators where the price already fully reprices margin (Endeavour, Silvercorp) and earlier-stage names where a sustained silver price would simply unlock financing that wasn't available at lower levels.

headline: WHY COPPER AT $14,800/T IS A DEMAND SIGNAL: One AI Factory Needs 50,000 Tonnes — Structural $15,000 Bull Case Builds
snippet: IndexBox's August 2026 analysis of the copper bull market argues that the record LME price of $14,455 per tonne is primarily a demand signal rather than a supply-shock event — citing S&P Global projections of 42 million metric tonnes of global demand by 2040 and the specific calculation that a 1-gigawatt AI data centre factory requires approximately 50,000 metric tonnes of copper for cabling, cooling, and power distribution systems. The analysis identifies the four simultaneous demand drivers that make copper's current pricing unusual: AI data centre build-out requiring massive copper intensity per facility; power grid upgrade spending in both the US and EU to electrify transportation and industry; pre-tariff US copper stockpiling by industrial buyers; and Chinese buyers competing for the same LME inventory, creating the cash-to-three-month backwardation that briefly widened to $207/tonne. For investors in copper development projects: the structural significance of the $14,800 price is not its exact level but the fact that S&P Global's demand models — projecting 42 million tonnes by 2040 from current production of approximately 22 million tonnes — require the market to fund roughly $1.5 trillion in new mine development over the next 15 years, creating a persistent M&A and project-financing environment that directly benefits copper juniors with resource-defined projects in bankable jurisdictions.

headline: SILVER OUTLOOK AUGUST 2026: Bull Case $90 on Fed Pause + Industrial Demand; Bear Case Needs Rate Hike Data Won't Support
snippet: Canadian Mining Report's August 2026 silver price analysis examines the bull and bear cases at $64/oz after silver's 11.31% gain over the past month and 69.08% year-over-year return — concluding the bull case is structurally stronger given that the Federal Reserve's September rate-hike probability has fallen to approximately 30% following four consecutive weeks of below-consensus macro data (payrolls, CPI, PPI, retail sales), while silver's industrial demand base from solar panels, electric vehicles, and AI data centre power systems is growing faster than production capacity. The bear case requires an active Federal Reserve tightening cycle that the current data sequence — four straight soft macro prints — makes increasingly difficult to justify without a reversal in the inflation trend; the analysis frames this as an asymmetric setup where the primary downside risk (a Fed hike) requires a reversal of existing macro conditions, while the primary upside case (Fed pause + sustained industrial demand) simply requires conditions to persist. For retail silver mining investors: the analysis argues that silver's 69% YoY gain has not yet been fully reflected in silver mining equity multiples, as even mid-tier silver producers are trading at 8–12x forward earnings versus the 20–30x multiples that characterized prior silver bull cycle peaks.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $87/LB: 20% YEAR-OVER-YEAR GAIN AS NUCLEAR BUILDOUT ACCELERATES — Enrichment Capacity Tightens
snippet: Uranium spot closed at $87.25 per pound on August 13, 2026, up 0.11% on the day and up 19.93% year-over-year — a price level that Sprott's uranium market analysis characterizes as structurally supported by a combination of 66 reactors under construction globally (the highest count since the 1970s), declining Russian enrichment market access as Western utilities continue diversifying away from Tenex contracts, and the continued constrained supply of new mined uranium given the lag between royalty streams, exploration capital, and actual mine production. Sweden's Uranium Law Reform, which took effect August 5, 2026, reinforces the multi-year policy shift toward uranium as a strategic energy asset in Europe — a continent that previously treated uranium mining as politically radioactive but is now actively developing domestic supply frameworks. For uranium investors: $87/lb represents a price where existing Athabasca Basin deposits generate compelling IRRs on new development, but where producing mines and royalty streams remain the most liquid exposure — a dynamic that maintains the strategic premium on proven Athabasca Basin exploration results like those emerging from active drill programs in Saskatchewan.

headline: MINRES BALD HILL: LITHIUM GUIDANCE DUE AUGUST 27 — First Official Production Metrics Since 18-Month Restart at 165,000 tpa SC6 Capacity
source_name: Discovery Alert / Mineral Resources Ltd. (ASX: MIN)
snippet: Mineral Resources Ltd. (ASX: MIN) has set August 27, 2026 as the date for releasing detailed FY27 guidance — covering expected sales volumes, free-on-board costs, and capital expenditure — for its Bald Hill lithium mine in Western Australia, which restarted following an 18-month care-and-maintenance period after lithium prices recovered from their 2024 lows. Bald Hill's production capacity stands at approximately 165,000 dry metric tonnes per annum of 5.1% spodumene concentrate (equivalent to 140,000 dmt SC6 per annum), the restart required A$20 million in reactivation capital, and first shipment from the Port of Esperance is targeted for Q1 FY27. For lithium investors: the August 27 guidance release is the first hard numerical framework for Bald Hill's economics under the current lithium price environment — lithium carbonate in China stands at 147,500 CNY/T, up approximately 80% year-over-year — and MinRes's decision to restart at this price level, and the specific cost guidance it provides, will serve as a real-world reference data point for the operating economics of WA hard-rock lithium mines that most junior resource models are still using as assumed inputs.
